title: Finite stratified local cohomological bounds become global
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning a scheme with a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $i_\alpha:S_\alpha\to X$ be a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] and choose a pro-étale covering $\{U_{\alpha j}\to S_\alpha\}_j$ on each stratum [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $R$ be any sheaf of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Restrict coefficients by their actual exact inverse images [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction]. Suppose for each $\alpha,j$ there are integers $a_{\alpha j}\leq b_{\alpha j}$ such that $H^q(K|_{U_{\alpha j}})=0$ outside $[a_{\alpha j},b_{\alpha j}]$. Then one may select finitely many quasi-compact open subschemes of the covering members whose composites still cover each stratum, and there are integers $a\leq b$ such that $H^q(K)=0$ for all $q\notin[a,b]$. One may take the minimum of the lower bounds and maximum of the upper bounds of their original covering members, with $[0,0]$ for an empty selected family. No flatness of $K$ and no dimension bound on $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.3 and Proposition 6.6.11, reverse implication; finite-cover boundedness argument. topology.tex Tag 04ZA (lemma-Noetherian-quasi-compact); pro-étale covering definition and finite-stratum detection.

proof.text: The Noetherian-scheme instances give a Noetherian underlying space and local Noetherianity of X. Install the immersion structures of S. Each stratum embeds in X, hence has Noetherian underlying space and is compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets]. It is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth], since an immersion is locally of finite type [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This also makes each stratum quasi-separated. Thus the compactness convention [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] applies without an extra hypothesis.

Apply QuasiCompactCover.exists_isAffineOpen_of_isCompact to the top open of each stratum and its given pro-etale cover [sk-def-pe-site]. This gives finitely many labels j and affine opens W in the original covering members, whose images cover the stratum. Their composites are weakly etale; they are quasi-compact because their sources are compact and the stratum is quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Therefore the finite family C of selected opens is a pro-etale cover, using QuasiCompactCover.of_finite. It has a refinement morphism to the finite family E of their original covering members. QuasiCompactCover.of_hom transfers quasi-compact covering from C to E, and E is jointly surjective with weakly etale component maps. Consequently E too is a pro-etale cover. This permits using the original local hypotheses directly, without composing derived inverse images along the open inclusions.

The sigma type of selected pairs (stratum, finite index) is finite. If inhabited, Finset.exists_min_image and Finset.exists_max_image give indices attaining the least selected lower endpoint and greatest selected upper endpoint. Let these be a and b. The original interval at the minimizing index shows a <= b. Every selected lower endpoint is >= a and every selected upper endpoint is <= b, so a degree outside [a,b] is outside every selected original interval. If the sigma type is empty, take a=b=0; the assertions on selected indices and attainment implications are vacuous. In the inhabited case, all m(alpha)=0 is impossible because the minimizing index has a second coordinate in Fin(m(alpha)).

Convert the finite locally closed stratification to Stratification.ofNoetherianSpace: its strata are constructible because X is Noetherian. Fix a degree q outside the common interval and let M=H^q(K). For each selected original member, exactness over the actual inverse-image ring [def-sfb-proetale-ring-derived-inverse-image] and the exact-functor cohomology comparison [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] identify the inverse image of M with H^q of the given derived inverse image of K, which is zero by the local hypothesis and the endpoint inequalities. Place M in degree zero. The exact-functor single-object comparison shows that its derived restrictions along the covers E are zero. Apply the unbounded derived zero-detection clause of [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-stratum-detection]. The resulting global degree-zero object is zero; applying H^0 and the single-object homology isomorphism gives M=0. The same argument handles an empty selected family, since the local premises are then vacuous. This proves exactly the stated global bounds with attained extrema, with no coefficient restriction beyond the original statement.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 6.6.11 reverse-implication locality argument, expanded using the existing finite affine refinement and derived stratum-detection declarations.
